newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics up on Samsung DRAM output cuts.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics up on Samsung DRAM output cuts.

text.p: Taiwan's electronics rose in early Friday trade on expected price rebounds for 16 megabit dynamic random access memory chips after South Korea's Samsung said on Thursday it would cut 16MB DRAM production.
After 50 minutes, electronics rose 1.06 percent, but off from early highs of more than two percent. Meanwhile, the overall index was up 0.76 percent.
Among electronics, semiconductor-related shares rose most, with Mosel Vitelic up 50 cents or 1.33 percent to T$38.2 and United Microelectronics up T$1 or 2.61 percent to T$39.3.
Brokers said the Samsung move would help price rebounds on 16MB DRAMs, but only in the short term.
"Samsung's move should help a short-term price rebounds on 16MB DRAMs," said Nomura Securities senior analyst Ben Lee.
"But as Samsung's capacity will transfer to produce 64MB DRAMs, prices on 64MB DRAMs then will fall, thus pulling down 16MB DRAM prices in the long run," Lee said.
Brokers said they did not expect a major recovery for the semiconductor industry before the third or fourth quarter.
